intro: Anthropic prompt caching gives ~90% discount on cached input tokens. For agents — where the system prompt + tool definitions are huge and re-sent every step — caching reshapes the cost math. Done well, you'll pay for context once per session, not once per turn.

items.title: How it works
items.whenToUse: Anytime your prompt has a stable prefix repeated across calls.
items.mechanism: Mark cache_control: { type: 'ephemeral' } at one or more positions in your system / tools / messages. The platform hashes everything UP TO that marker; on the next call with the same prefix, you pay 10% for the cached portion + full price only for what's new.
items.tradeoff: First call writes the cache (slightly more expensive than uncached). Subsequent hits within the TTL pay the discount.

items.title: TTL: 5 minutes or 1 hour
items.mechanism: 5-minute default. 1-hour available (beta header). After TTL, cache is gone — next call re-writes. Cache hit requires byte-identical prefix.
items.tradeoff: 5m fits bursty agent traffic. 1h fits sparse, repeated workflows (long-running agents, daily batch jobs).

items.title: Breakpoint placement — the 4-marker pattern
items.mechanism: Place markers at: (1) end of system prompt, (2) end of tool definitions, (3) end of conversation up through the previous turn, (4) just before the latest user/tool-result message. Markers cumulate — each marks a cumulative-prefix cache point.
items.tradeoff: Maximum reuse. The latest turn is never cached because it's the new content. As the conversation grows, breakpoint (3) keeps absorbing more.

items.title: The economics
items.mechanism: If your agent makes N tool-loop calls per session with a P-token static prefix, total static-prefix cost without caching = N * P * price_in. With caching: P * 1.25 (write) + (N-1) * P * 0.10 * price_in. Break-even at N=2 in almost all cases.
items.tradeoff: Any agent that loops at all benefits. The longer the system + tool defs, the larger the savings — easily 70–85% off input on long agent runs.

items.title: Invalidation traps
items.mechanism: Cache key is byte-identical prefix. A whitespace change, a tool description edit, a model bump — all invalidate. Coordinate edits to maximize cache reuse.
items.tradeoff: Treat cached prefixes as immutable contracts. Version them; don't bikeshed copy.

items.title: What can't be cached
items.mechanism: The CURRENT turn's user content is never cached. Tool RESULTS are part of the new content. Cache works on PREFIXES, not arbitrary spans.
items.tradeoff: Frame your loop so the cacheable parts (system, tools, prior turns) come before the new parts (current user message, current tool result).

pitfalls.title: Forgetting the marker
pitfalls.body: Caching is opt-in. Without cache_control on at least one position, you pay full price every turn even though the prefix is identical.

pitfalls.title: System-prompt bikeshedding
pitfalls.body: Every tweak invalidates the cache for every running session. Pin the wording, version it like an API.

pitfalls.title: Marker at end of conversation
pitfalls.body: Marker at the end of CURRENT user message → caches nothing useful (no future call has that exact prefix). Marker goes BEFORE volatile content.

pitfalls.title: Volatile tool definitions
pitfalls.body: Tool definitions that include dynamic data (current time, user's row) invalidate every call. Move dynamic data out of tool DEFS into tool RESULTS.

pitfalls.title: Prefix below minimum
pitfalls.body: Anthropic requires cached blocks to meet a token minimum (1024 for Sonnet, 2048 for Opus as of writing). Tiny prefixes can't be cached — group them.
